messages:
Ava (product): Quick sync — small exploration for the playground chat controls. Goal: a compact top bar that covers streaming indicator, a single stop/regenerate control (stateful), a micro token-readout, and fast access to prompt library. Mock in Figma: https://figma.com/s/compact-playground (preview).

Sam (design): Love the compact approach. Two quick UX questions: 1) Stop vs Stop+Regenerate — do we show one button that toggles or two adjacent buttons? 2) Token readout: inline next to input or behind a hover?

Ruth (eng): From infra/runtime POV we prefer single control that switches: less event churn (stop -> regen = single API flow). But need clear affordance so users don't accidentally regen while streaming. Suggest a split-tap behavior: primary click = Stop, long-press or secondary menu = Regenerate.

Kai (devex): Keyboard accessibility note: any long-press pattern must have keyboard equivalent (e.g., Enter to stop, then Ctrl+Enter to regenerate). Also need clear ARIA labels for streaming region so screen readers know tokens are coming.

Sam (design): Good point. New proposal: a single rounded pill with two visual states: "Stop" (red dot + label) while streaming; when stopped it becomes "Regenerate" (arrow icon). Tooltip: "Press Enter to stop; Press ⌘+Enter to regenerate". Token readout as a small live-updating counter on the right of the input, condensed like "312 / 4k".

Ruth (eng): Implementation notes: streaming indicator should be a separate visually minimal element — animated pulse inside the message area not in the button. That keeps the button stable and reduces layout shift. We can emit a small `aria-live="polite"` update for the counter.

Ava (product): Accessibility nit: token counter must have text alternative: "Tokens used: 312 of 4096" for screen readers. Also color contrast for the stop state is important (red alone insufficient). Add icon + text.

Kai (devex): For the prompt library quick access, can we add a keyboard shortcut ("L") that opens a mini-panel? This saves mouse trips. It should be discoverable via the command palette too. Also confirm focus flow: opening library should not steal focus from input unless user explicitly chooses a prompt.

Sam (design): Agree. Mini-panel layout idea: 3 columns on desktop, collapsible to a bottom sheet on mobile. We'll mock header with "Recent / Favorites / Explore" tabs. Quick apply button should show a confirmation toast with an undo to avoid accidental overwrites.

Ruth (eng): Edge case: applying a prompt while stream is active — do we queue it or interrupt? My vote: queue and notify the user. Queue UI could live in the button tooltip: "Queued: 1".

Ava (product): UX copy proposed for the button tooltip states: "Click to stop streaming. After stopping, click Regenerate to rerun the request with current input." Short and clear. Add a secondary line for keyboard shortcuts. Thoughts?

Kai (devex): Suggest shorter: "Stop streaming — then Regenerate (⌘+Enter)." Keep tooltips one-liners ideally. Longer explanation can be in a help bubble.

Sam (design): Accessibility checklist for this iteration: 1) visible focus ring on button 2) ARIA roles for the stream region 3) token counter exposed via aria-live and hidden text 4) keyboard shortcuts documented in help. I'll add to the Figma notes.

Ruth (eng): Small dev note: backend will expose these states via `streamState: streaming | stopped | queued` and `tokenCount` in the session websocket. Example quick payload:```json
{ "streamState": "streaming", "tokenCount": 312 }
``` Keep payload minimal to avoid extra CPU.

UI Bot: deploy-preview available: https://preview.redwood/dev/compact-playground/1772001234 (auto screenshot attached).

Ava (product): Next steps: Sam to iterate designs with the split visual (pulse separate from button), Kai to spec keyboard mappings, Ruth to confirm socket events and debounce strategy, and me to write copy and confirm tooltips. Ping back by EOD tomorrow. :thumbsup:
